purpose: How a business internet and wireless agent turns activated accounts into a durable compensated book - tracking activation, residual and account-based compensation as verifiable program mechanisms, reconciling and disputing carrier statements, containing clawback exposure, timing renewals and technology refreshes, reading and answering churn, serving as the honest escalation layer between customer and carrier, and growing multi-stream accounts while program compliance and disclosure-first conduct protect both the customer relationship and the compensation stream.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

carrier partner-program terms, compensation plans and product availability change without notice; every lifecycle commitment (renewal, save offer, expansion, win-back) presumes a same-cycle check of the current program documents, never a remembered version

the default channel model is agency: the carrier bills the customer, provides tier-one support, and owns the retail account; the agent is compensated under the program agreement and operates as the relationship and escalation layer, never as the carrier

compensation is described only as mechanism classes (activation/upfront, residual/ongoing, account-based, chargeback/clawback) and qualitative bands; no specific commission rate, price, fee amount, or account multiple is ever stated as fact

content is educational and operational for the agent-operator, not personalized financial, legal, tax, or insurance advice; program-specific and jurisdiction-specific obligations must be verified against the current agreement and local rules before acting
exclusions: channel-model comparison, program entry qualification, master-agent selection, carrier portfolio strategy, initial bundle architecture and needs-discovery methodology for new customers - that is the carrier programs and bundle strategy KB upstream

address-level serviceability and coverage checks, site surveys, ordering, provisioning and activation coordination, failover configuration and testing, and install handoff - that is the site qualification and activation KB; any lifecycle event that changes an address, a technology, or a service footprint routes back through it

stating specific commission rates, residual percentages, prices, early-termination amounts, clawback figures, or account revenue multiples as fact; compensation and cost mechanics appear only as mechanisms and qualitative bands with a per-deal verification path
any representation that the agent is the carrier, controls carrier pricing, or holds authority the current program agreement does not grant
fear-selling, pressure retention tactics, or exploiting a customer's outage or financial distress to force a decision; personalized financial, legal, or tax advice to the customer or the operator

assuming serviceability or coverage for any refresh, relocation, expansion, or win-back - serviceability is address-specific fact-finding performed by the site-qualification process, never assumed from memory or a coverage map alone

competency_questions.question: Through which mechanisms does compensation actually arrive on each account - activation, residual, account-based - and how do I track expectations without inventing figures?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMP_MECHANISM_LEDGER maps every active service to its mechanism class, program version and expected-payment schedule sourced from current program documents, and PROGRAM_TERMS_CURRENCY supplies the verification discipline that keeps those expectations current rather than remembered

competency_questions.question: How do I catch a missing, short, or misclassified commission payment, and what turns a variance into a recovered payment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STATEMENT_RECONCILIATION describes the cycle-by-cycle match of carrier statements against ledger expectations with variance classes, and COMP_DISCREPANCY_DISPUTE describes the evidence pack, filing channel, and deadline discipline that recovers the money

competency_questions.question: What events can claw back compensation already paid, and how do I keep that exposure down instead of just absorbing it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLAWBACK_EXPOSURE_CONTROL names the trigger classes and window mechanics per program and the containment levers, and POST_ACTIVATION_INTAKE shows how first-bill review and early onboarding touches prevent the early cancels that trigger most clawbacks

competency_questions.question: When does a newly activated account become my lifecycle responsibility, and what must intake capture before the install team moves on?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POST_ACTIVATION_INTAKE defines the intake record - activation confirmation, services and terms as sold, expected compensation entries, first-bill check, and the first onboarding touch - as the gate between activation and lifecycle management

competency_questions.question: How do I know which contracts are approaching renewal or auto-renewal, and how do I run a renewal conversation that is disclosure-first rather than a silent rollover?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTRACT_RENEWAL_RADAR supplies the per-service term calendar and work-back schedule, and RENEWAL_PLAY_DESIGN supplies the verified-current-offer, right-sized, plainly-disclosed renewal play built before the auto-renew date

competency_questions.question: How do technology retirements and refresh cycles - copper shutdown, fiber overbuild, wireless generation changes - move through my book, and when do they force re-qualification?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TECH_REFRESH_CYCLE treats each retirement or build-out as an enumerated book event with a verified compensation class and an explicit route through address-level re-qualification before anything is promised

competency_questions.question: What early signals predict that an account is going to churn, and which of them are actionable rather than noise?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHURN_SIGNAL_WATCH lists the signal classes (ticket clusters, billing disputes, competitor build at the address, non-response, payment lateness, business distress) with a triage rule, and ACCOUNT_HEALTH_REGISTER supplies the per-account substrate those signals are read from

competency_questions.question: What am I allowed to offer to save an at-risk account, where does my authority end, and when does a save go to the carrier's retention desk?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAVE_PLAY_WITHIN_PROGRAM distinguishes agent-side fixes from carrier-authority offers and routes pricing concessions to the retention desk, and PROGRAM_COMPLIANCE_SHIELD marks the authority boundary that no save promise may cross

competency_questions.question: When is a lost account worth winning back, and what do the program's win-back and re-entry rules mean for compensation before I spend the effort?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WINBACK_PIPELINE requires the current program's win-back compensation mechanism and eligibility window to be verified first, then sizes the effort against the loss reason and routes any address or technology change through re-qualification

competency_questions.question: What do I handle myself versus route to the carrier when the customer calls me first, and how do I stay honest about who I am and who owns the account?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ESCALATION_INTAKE_TRIAGE gives the intake and triage rule with the affiliation-honesty script, and CARRIER_ESCALATION_NAVIGATION gives the partner-channel machinery for driving the carrier to resolution with a documented trail

competency_questions.question: How do I turn an outage or failover event into retained trust rather than churn, without fear-selling the customer into upgrades?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OUTAGE_AND_FAILOVER_AFTERCARE describes the during-event communication and post-event review that earns trust, and DISCLOSURE_FIRST_LIFECYCLE_CONDUCT supplies the no-fear-selling and vulnerable-customer rules that bound any follow-on recommendation

competency_questions.question: How do I grow one account into additional revenue streams at lifecycle moments without over-selling services the customer does not need?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MULTI_STREAM_EXPANSION ties every attach to a documented need surfaced at a lifecycle moment and to current program authorization, and PERIODIC_ACCOUNT_REVIEW supplies the honest usage-and-fit review those needs are surfaced in - including right-sizing down

competency_questions.question: What conduct forfeits compensation or the agreement itself, and how do I protect the book's continuity against program and partner changes I do not control?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROGRAM_COMPLIANCE_SHIELD names the forfeiture classes (unauthorized products, misrepresentation, order manipulation, branding misuse) with prevention practices, and AGREEMENT_CONTINUITY_RISK covers residual survivability, change notices, minimum-production conditions, and the diversification response

competency_questions.question: What does the health of the whole book look like - mechanism mix, carrier concentration, churn trend - and where should lifecycle effort go next?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PORTFOLIO_MIX_DASHBOARD rolls the ledger and reconciliation history into a mechanism-mix, concentration, and churn-trend view expressed in qualitative bands, and states how that view redirects renewal, retention, and expansion effort

glossary.definition: An upfront payment mechanism triggered once by a completed, carrier-confirmed activation of a service; its amount, conditions, and payment timing are defined by the program plan in force at the sale and must be verified per deal, never assumed.

A recurring payment mechanism that continues while the customer's account stays active and billing, typically keyed to billed revenue or a per-service schedule under the current plan; it is the annuity component of the book and stops or changes when the account, the plan, or the agreement changes.

A mechanism keyed to the overall account relationship - total billed services, account growth, or tiered account value - rather than to a single service activation; programs use it to reward multi-service depth on one customer.

A mechanism that reverses compensation already paid when a defined trigger occurs inside a defined window - most commonly early disconnect, non-payment disconnect, order cancellation, or fraud flag; the window length and trigger list are program-specific and must be read from the current agreement.

The cycle-by-cycle matching of the carrier's or master agent's reported payments against the agent's own expected-payment ledger, producing a variance list of missing, short, late, or misclassified lines to be disputed inside the program's dispute window.

A contract mechanism that rolls a service term forward automatically unless notice is given before a cutoff date; its notice window and renewal terms vary by agreement and are exactly what a disclosure-first renewal conversation must surface before the rollover happens.

A forced or elective migration moment in the book - copper or legacy-circuit retirement, a fiber overbuild reaching the customer's street, a wireless generation change, or end-of-support equipment - that reopens design, requires address-level re-qualification, and usually carries its own compensation class under the program.

The program-defined period and conditions under which re-acquiring a churned customer is treated differently from a new sale - compensation may be reduced, delayed, or void if the customer returns too soon or under the same account; it must be verified before win-back effort is spent.

The agent's standing role between customer and carrier: fielding the customer's issues first, triaging what the agent can resolve against what must go to carrier support, and driving carrier tickets through partner channels - all without ever implying the agent is the carrier.

The full set of active accounts whose compensation flows to the agent under one or more program agreements; it is the asset that lifecycle management protects, and its value is a function of residual durability, churn, concentration, and agreement survivability - expressed in bands, never invented multiples.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for account_compensation_and_lifecycle_management work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Accept each newly activated account from the activation process into lifecycle management through a deliberate intake gate rather than by default. Intake captures the activation confirmation, the services and contract terms exactly as sold, the program and plan version the deal was written under, the expected compensation entries it should generate, and the install notes that matter later (equipment installed, failover arrangement, site contacts). It then runs the first-bill review - comparing the customer's first carrier invoice against what was quoted - because first-bill surprises are the single most preventable seed of early cancels, clawbacks, and lost trust, and schedules the first onboarding touch while goodwill from the install is still warm.

included: intake record with services, terms, and plan version as sold
excluded: the install and failover testing itself (activation KB)
ongoing statement reconciliation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: clawback or early-churn post-mortems show first-bill errors or missing intake data as a recurring cause

pros.claim: A first-bill review catches billing surprises while they are still correctable goodwill moments instead of cancellation triggers
pros.example: spotting an unrequested add-on charge on a bakery's first internet invoice and having the carrier correct it before the owner ever calls angry

cons.claim: A heavyweight intake ritual delays the account into lifecycle care and tempts skipping when install volume spikes
cons.example: a week of installs piling up unintaken, so a mis-billed dental office rides two bad invoices before anyone looks

failure_modes: treating activation as the finish line so no one owns the account until it complains
seeding compensation expectations from memory of the deal instead of the written order and plan version
skipping the first-bill review and meeting the billing error only as a cancellation call
acceptance_tests: every activated account has an intake record with services, term, plan version, expected compensation entries, and a completed first-bill check before it is considered under lifecycle management
revisit_triggers: an early cancel or clawback traces to a missed first-bill error
the activation handoff artifact changes shape

nodes.definition: Maintain verified currency on every program's compensation plan and terms, because carrier partner programs change compensation mechanisms, product availability, and rules without the agent's consent and often with thin notice. The discipline: keep a register of each carried program's current plan version and effective date; read change notices the cycle they arrive; and before any lifecycle commitment - a renewal quote, a save offer, an expansion attach, a win-back - re-verify the relevant terms in the current program documents rather than relying on what the plan said last quarter. Expected compensation is always expressed as the mechanism the current plan defines plus a verification path, never as a remembered or invented figure.

excluded: choosing which programs to carry (programs KB)
the reconciliation of paid statements

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier or master agent publishes a compensation plan revision, product change, or agreement amendment

pros.claim: Same-cycle verification prevents commitments priced on a dead plan version
pros.example: catching that the current plan moved a service from upfront-plus-residual to residual-only before quoting a renewal on the old assumption

cons.claim: Re-verifying before every commitment adds friction that tempts shortcuts on routine deals
cons.example: skipping the check on a familiar-looking renewal the same month the carrier quietly rewrote its term-length rules

failure_modes: quoting a customer or projecting income from a remembered plan version
letting change notices accumulate unread until a statement variance reveals them
treating one carrier's mechanics as true of another program
acceptance_tests: every carried program has a register entry with current plan version, effective date, and last-verified date, and every lifecycle commitment references a same-cycle terms check
revisit_triggers: a program change notice arrives
a statement variance suggests an unnoticed plan change
a new product appears in or vanishes from the program catalog

nodes.definition: Bind every lifecycle conversation to three conduct rules that are the ethical spine of the subdomain. Disclosure-first: term length, auto-renewal mechanics, early-termination consequences as a mechanism class, and what changes on renewal are stated plainly before any signature, not discovered later. No fear-selling: outages, competitor scare stories, or technology-retirement deadlines are never exaggerated to force an upgrade or a renewal; urgency claims must match verifiable fact. Vulnerable-customer care: a small-business owner in visible distress - financial trouble, an active outage, a family crisis - gets honest right-sizing and time to decide, not a pressure close; consent is documented and cooling-off norms are honored where they apply, with jurisdiction-specific rules verified rather than assumed.

included: pre-signature disclosure of term, auto-renew, and exit mechanics
excluded: the design of renewal or save offers themselves
personalized legal or financial advice to the customer

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a conduct complaint, a carrier compliance bulletin, or a change in applicable consumer-protection rules

pros.claim: Plain disclosure before signature converts renewals into trust deposits instead of future disputes
pros.example: walking a restaurant owner through exactly what auto-renewal would have rolled them into, and winning the next three referrals because of it

cons.claim: Full disclosure occasionally loses a deal that pressure would have closed
cons.example: a customer who declines a term renewal after hearing the exit mechanics clearly, staying month-to-month at lower commitment

failure_modes: letting an auto-renewal roll silently because the conversation felt awkward
using a copper-retirement date as a scare lever beyond what the carrier actually announced
pressure-closing a struggling owner into a longer term because the residual needs it
acceptance_tests: every renewal, save, expansion, and win-back interaction shows term and exit mechanics disclosed before commitment, urgency claims traceable to verifiable fact, and documented consent
revisit_triggers: a complaint or dispute alleges non-disclosure or pressure
consumer-protection or telemarketing rules in an operating jurisdiction change

nodes.definition: Treat program compliance as the shield around the entire compensation stream, because under an agency agreement the fastest way to lose the book is not churn but forfeiture. The forfeiture classes to guard: selling products or serving customer types the current agreement does not authorize; misrepresenting carrier affiliation in marketing, signage, or conversation; manipulating orders (splitting orders to multiply activation payments, self-dealing, activating services the customer did not knowingly order); misusing carrier branding outside program guidelines; and breaching data-handling or conduct rules the agreement incorporates. Each class is prevented by practice - authorization checks before offering, approved-marketing review, order integrity matching the customer's documented consent - and violations are treated as existential rather than as fine print.

excluded: negotiating agreement terms (programs KB)
customer-side disclosure conduct (covered by the conduct node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a compliance bulletin, audit notice, or agreement amendment changes what conduct forfeits compensation

pros.claim: Authorization checks before offers prevent the compensation-voiding sale that looks like a win
pros.example: declining to sell a camera add-on the program catalog no longer authorizes, instead of activating it and forfeiting the whole order's compensation

cons.claim: Strict compliance discipline slows opportunistic deals and can feel like leaving money on the table
cons.example: waiting a cycle to confirm a new product's authorization while a competitor quotes it immediately

failure_modes: selling an unauthorized product and voiding compensation on the entire order
marketing that implies the agent is the carrier and draws a compliance action
order manipulation that triggers audit, clawback of the book, or termination for cause
acceptance_tests: every offer traces to a current-program authorization check, marketing materials carry approved affiliation language, and every order matches the customer's documented consent
revisit_triggers: the program publishes new compliance guidelines or audit findings
a product's authorization status changes
any carrier inquiry into an order's integrity

nodes.definition: Build and maintain the ledger that makes compensation trackable: for every account, every active service mapped to its compensation mechanism class (activation/upfront, residual/ongoing, account-based), the program and plan version it was sold under, the expected-payment schedule the current plan defines, the clawback window status, and the payment state (pending, paying, disputed, clawed back, ended). Amounts are carried as plan-referenced expectations with a verification path to the program document, never as invented figures typed from memory. The ledger is the single substrate that reconciliation, clawback containment, and the portfolio view all read from - without it the agent is auditing the carrier's homework with no answer key.

excluded: the reconciliation act itself
portfolio-level roll-ups

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any change to services, plan versions, or payment states that the ledger has not yet absorbed

pros.claim: A plan-linked ledger turns 'the check feels small' into a specific, disputable line-item variance
pros.example: showing that a plumbing company's backup-wireless line stopped appearing on statements in the month the account was migrated between carrier billing systems

cons.claim: Ledger upkeep is unglamorous recurring work that decays quietly when skipped
cons.example: six months of unrecorded plan changes making the ledger's expectations as unreliable as no ledger at all

failure_modes: carrying expected amounts as remembered figures with no plan reference
not recording which plan version a deal was written under, making later disputes unarguable
letting ended services linger as phantom expectations that mask real variances
acceptance_tests: every active service on every account has a ledger entry with mechanism class, plan version, expected schedule referenced to the program document, clawback window status, and current payment state
revisit_triggers: a plan version changes for any carried program
a service is added, changed, or disconnected on any account
reconciliation reveals a ledger expectation that was wrong

nodes.definition: Maintain the operating record that lifecycle work reads from: per account, the services in place and their contract end and auto-renew dates, installed equipment and its age and technology generation, the support-ticket and outage history, payment behavior, site and contact changes, and notes from every review and escalation. This register is deliberately separate from the compensation ledger - one tracks what the agent is paid, the other tracks how the customer is doing - because conflating them tempts the agent to read every customer question through a commission lens. Renewal radar, churn watch, refresh planning, and escalation triage are all consumers of this one substrate, so its completeness and freshness bound the quality of everything downstream.

excluded: compensation amounts and payment states (ledger)
address-level serviceability data (activation KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: register data proves stale during a renewal, escalation, or churn event

pros.claim: One current register lets every lifecycle motion start from facts instead of archaeology
pros.example: opening a renewal conversation already knowing the customer logged four outage tickets last quarter and got a router swap in March

cons.claim: A register that is not maintained becomes confidently wrong, which is worse than absent
cons.example: calling to discuss a contract end date that a mid-term amendment moved a year out, and losing credibility with the office manager

failure_modes: contract dates entered at intake and never updated after amendments
ticket history living only in email threads where triage cannot see patterns
treating the register as optional paperwork until a churn surprise proves otherwise
acceptance_tests: each account's register entry carries current contract dates, equipment generation, and a ticket and payment history complete enough to run renewal radar and churn triage without external lookup
revisit_triggers: any service change, amendment, escalation, or review touches an account
a lifecycle motion is caught working from stale register data

nodes.definition: Reconcile every commission statement from every carrier or master agent against the ledger's expectations, every cycle, inside the program's dispute window. The match classifies each expected entry as paid-as-expected, short-paid, missing, late, misclassified (paid under the wrong mechanism or rate class), or unexpected (paid but not expected - which can signal someone else's error that will be clawed back later). Variances are logged with the statement line, the ledger expectation, and the plan reference, then routed to dispute or to ledger correction. The discipline matters because unreconciled cycles compound: most programs bar disputes after a defined window, so a skipped month can convert a recoverable variance into a permanent write-off.

excluded: the dispute filing itself
renegotiating plan terms

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new statement arrives, a variance recurs, or the program's statement format or dispute terms change

pros.claim: Cycle-complete reconciliation catches quiet residual drop-offs that would otherwise bleed for months
pros.example: noticing a veterinary clinic's residual line vanished after the carrier merged two billing systems, within the same month it happened

cons.claim: Line-by-line reconciliation of small statements can cost more attention than the variances it recovers
cons.example: an hour spent chasing a rounding-level mismatch on a single-line account while a renewal window closes unworked

failure_modes: skipping cycles until the dispute window has closed on the missed variances
reconciling against remembered amounts rather than plan-referenced ledger expectations
banking unexpected payments silently and meeting them again as clawbacks
acceptance_tests: every statement cycle ends with each expected entry classified, every variance logged with statement line and plan reference, and no variance older than the program's dispute window left unfiled
revisit_triggers: a variance class recurs across cycles for the same program
a statement format or delivery system changes
the dispute-window terms change

nodes.definition: Convert reconciliation variances into recovered compensation through disciplined dispute work. Each dispute carries an evidence pack - the signed order or documented consent, the carrier's activation confirmation, the ledger entry with its plan-version reference, and the statement line showing the shortfall - filed through the program's designated dispute channel (portal, partner support queue, or the master agent's commissions desk) before the dispute deadline. Open disputes are tracked with aging and escalation steps: unanswered disputes get re-escalated on a schedule, patterns of identical variances get bundled into a single systemic case, and outcomes are written back to the ledger so the same error class is caught faster next cycle. The tone stays professional and evidence-led; the dispute channel is kept separate from customer-service escalations so a commissions fight never degrades a customer's ticket.

excluded: customer-facing service escalations
legal action against a carrier (beyond scope; seek counsel)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: dispute outcomes, response-time drift, or a change in the program's dispute process

pros.claim: Evidence-led disputes recover money and train the carrier's commissions desk to take the agent's filings seriously
pros.example: a bundled dispute showing the same missing backup-wireless residual across nine accounts getting fixed at the system level in one case

cons.claim: Dispute volume has a relationship cost when it reads as adversarial rather than accurate
cons.example: a partner manager who starts slow-walking requests after a barrage of small, poorly evidenced disputes

failure_modes: filing past the deadline and converting a recoverable variance into a write-off
disputing without the plan-version reference and losing on 'current plan says otherwise'
mixing commissions disputes into customer-service channels where they stall both
acceptance_tests: every dispute has a complete evidence pack, a filing timestamp inside the deadline, an aging status with a next escalation step, and a resolved outcome written back to the ledger
revisit_triggers: a dispute ages past its expected response time
the same variance class recurs after a 'fixed' outcome
the program changes its dispute channel or deadline

nodes.definition: Manage clawback as an exposure to be contained, not a tax to be absorbed. Know each program's trigger classes - early disconnect inside the clawback window, non-payment disconnect, order cancellation before install, downgrade below a qualifying tier, fraud or quality flags - and the window mechanics that govern them, all read from the current agreement. Containment works on both ends: before activation, honest qualification and expectation-setting reduce the deals that were never going to stick (a feedback the agent sends upstream to discovery and design); after activation, the intake first-bill review, early onboarding touches, and fast response to first-90-day trouble keep fragile accounts alive through the window. The ledger tracks each entry's window status so the agent knows at any moment how much paid compensation is still reversible, expressed as an exposure band rather than a false-precision figure.

included: trigger-class and window mechanics per program
early-tenure care to prevent trigger events
upstream feedback on deals that keep clawing back
excluded: the qualification and discovery methodology itself (programs KB)
disputing an incorrectly applied clawback (dispute node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: clawback lines on statements, window or trigger changes in the program, or a cohort pattern emerging

pros.claim: Window-status tracking converts clawback from ambush into a managed, banded exposure
pros.example: knowing that a quarter's activation payments are still inside their windows before deciding to fund new equipment purchases from them

cons.claim: Over-focusing on clawback avoidance can bias the agent against serving legitimately risky small customers
cons.example: declining a young food truck's connectivity deal solely because new businesses disconnect more often

failure_modes: spending activation compensation as final money while it is still inside the window
discovering trigger classes only from the first clawback line on a statement
ignoring the pattern that one deal profile keeps generating clawbacks
acceptance_tests: every ledger entry carries its clawback window status, an aggregate in-window exposure band exists, and early-tenure accounts have scheduled onboarding touches through their windows
revisit_triggers: a clawback arrives whose trigger class was not on the map
the program changes window length or trigger definitions
a cohort's clawback pattern points at an upstream qualification gap

nodes.definition: Run the calendar that ensures no contract end or auto-renewal date arrives unannounced. Every service term in the book sits on a radar with its end date, its auto-renew mechanics and notice cutoff, and a work-back schedule that opens the renewal motion early enough to verify current offers, review usage fit, and hold an unhurried disclosure-first conversation before the cutoff - not the week the term lapses. The radar also watches the dates the agent does not control: promotional pricing roll-offs that will spike the customer's bill (a churn trigger the agent should surface before the customer discovers it angrily), and carrier-side term amendments recorded from escalations or amendments. Radar discipline is what makes renewals a planned play rather than a scramble.

included: term and auto-renew calendar with notice cutoffs
work-back scheduling ahead of each date
promo roll-off and amendment date tracking
excluded: the renewal offer design itself
new-customer contract negotiation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a missed cutoff, a bill-shock call the radar should have preempted, or amendment data arriving late

pros.claim: A work-back schedule buys the time that separates a considered renewal from a deadline scramble
pros.example: opening a print shop's renewal two billing cycles before its auto-renew cutoff, with usage data and current offers already pulled

cons.claim: Radar dates are only as good as the amendments fed into them
cons.example: a mid-term upgrade that reset a term length without the radar being told, making the whole work-back schedule wrong

failure_modes: auto-renew cutoffs discovered after they pass
promo roll-offs surfacing as the customer's angry bill-shock call instead of the agent's proactive heads-up
renewal conversations habitually starting inside the notice window under time pressure
acceptance_tests: every service term in the book appears on the radar with end date, auto-renew cutoff, and a work-back start date that precedes the cutoff by a stated margin
revisit_triggers: an amendment or upgrade changes any term date
a renewal is caught starting inside its notice window

nodes.definition: Design each renewal as a fresh, verified, right-sized proposal rather than a rubber stamp of the expiring term. The play starts from a same-cycle check of the current program's offers and renewal compensation mechanics (renewal events often pay under a different mechanism than new activations - verify, never assume parity), reads the account's actual usage and trouble history, and decides what to propose: same service renewed, an upgrade the usage genuinely justifies, a downgrade if the customer is over-provisioned, or a shorter term when a technology refresh is plausibly close. The conversation itself is disclosure-first - what changes, what the term commits the customer to, what auto-renewal would otherwise have done - and the outcome is documented with consent. A renewal proposed on stale offers or silent rollover is treated as a defect even when it happens to close.

excluded: silent auto-rollover as a strategy
new-service bundle design for prospects (programs KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: renewal outcomes, offer changes, or evidence that right-sizing decisions are being skipped under volume

pros.claim: Right-sized renewals hold accounts far longer than maximized ones
pros.example: moving an over-provisioned insurance office down a bandwidth tier at renewal and keeping the account when a door-knocking competitor leads with price

cons.claim: A fresh verified play per renewal costs real effort compared to letting auto-renewal run
cons.example: a fifty-account renewal quarter where each play needs an offer check, usage read, and a scheduled conversation

failure_modes: assuming renewal compensation matches new-activation mechanics and mispricing the play
proposing from last quarter's offer sheet the month after the program restructured it
locking a long term weeks before a fiber overbuild makes the design obsolete
acceptance_tests: every renewal play shows a same-cycle offer and mechanism check, a usage-fit decision with rationale (including downgrade considered), and a documented disclosure-first close or an explicit customer decision to let the term lapse
revisit_triggers: the program changes renewal compensation mechanics or offers
a refresh event moves onto an account mid-play
usage data contradicts the proposed tier

nodes.definition: Manage the technology clock ticking under every account: carrier retirements of copper and legacy circuits, fiber overbuilds reaching the customer's street, wireless generation transitions that obsolete installed backup hardware, and end-of-support equipment aging in closets. The work is to enumerate which accounts each announced event touches (from the health register's equipment and technology data), verify what the current program pays on migration or refresh events as a mechanism class, and open each affected account's refresh conversation early enough to plan rather than panic - always routing the actual feasibility question through address-level re-qualification, because an overbuild map or a retirement notice is not a serviceability fact for a specific suite. Refresh events are also the natural, honest moment to revisit design; they are never inflated into false-deadline pressure beyond what the carrier actually announced.

included: retirement and build-out event tracking against the book
affected-account enumeration by equipment and technology
excluded: performing serviceability checks or site surveys (activation KB)
using retirement dates as scare leverage

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a retirement, overbuild, or generation-change announcement, or a slip in a previously announced timeline

pros.claim: Enumerating affected accounts the day an event is announced converts a forced migration into a planned book-wide play
pros.example: listing every account on legacy circuits the morning a retirement notice lands, and opening conversations a year before the shutoff

cons.claim: Refresh planning on announced-but-slipping carrier timelines can trigger premature migrations
cons.example: moving a customer off a working circuit for a retirement date the carrier then postponed twice

failure_modes: learning about a retirement from a customer's disconnection notice instead of tracking it
promising a fiber migration from an overbuild map without re-qualifying the address
assuming a migration pays like a new activation when the program treats it as a plan change
acceptance_tests: every announced retirement or build-out touching the book has an affected-account list, a verified refresh compensation class, and per-account plans that route through re-qualification before any commitment
revisit_triggers: a carrier announces or reschedules a retirement, build-out, or generation transition
installed equipment in the register crosses an end-of-support date

nodes.definition: Hold a periodic review with each account that examines fit rather than pitches product: does actual usage match the provisioned bandwidth, has the backup connection been exercised and did it perform, have staff counts, locations, hours, or the business itself changed, and is anything on the bill going unused. The review's integrity comes from its willingness to conclude 'you are paying for more than you need' - honest right-sizing down is what makes the review welcome and makes its occasional 'you have genuinely outgrown this' credible. Findings feed three consumers: the health register (facts), the renewal play (fit decisions), and the expansion pipeline (documented needs) - and the review cadence scales with account complexity, denser for multi-site accounts, lighter for stable single-service ones.

included: findings routed to register, renewal, and expansion
excluded: the expansion close itself
site surveys or technical audits (activation KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: review outcomes drifting toward pure sales conversations, or fit findings contradicting current provisioning

pros.claim: Reviews that sometimes recommend paying less are the ones customers keep attending
pros.example: cutting an unused static-IP block from a florist's bill at review, and being the first call when she opens a second shop

cons.claim: Reviews across a whole book are recurring time that stable accounts may not visibly repay
cons.example: an afternoon of well-run reviews on quiet single-line accounts producing no change at all that quarter

failure_modes: reviews that are transparently sales calls and train customers to decline them
never re-examining backup performance until the outage that proves it was misconfigured
findings discussed but never written back, so the next motion starts ignorant
acceptance_tests: each completed review records usage-versus-provisioned findings, a right-sizing conclusion in either direction with rationale, and write-backs to the register plus any renewal or expansion routing
revisit_triggers: an account's business circumstances change materially between cadenced reviews
review findings repeatedly contradict provisioned service levels

nodes.definition: Watch each account for the signals that precede a cancellation and triage them while intervention is still possible. The signal classes: clustered or repeated trouble tickets (especially unresolved ones), a billing dispute or bill-shock event, a competitor's build or door-knocking campaign reaching the customer's address or plaza, payment lateness shifting from occasional to patterned, non-response from a previously engaged contact, visible business distress (shortened hours, staff cuts, for-lease signage), and structural events like relocation, sale of the business, or franchise conversion. Triage separates actionable signals (a fixable service problem, a bill error, a competitor offer the program can answer) from structural ones (business closing) where the honest play is a graceful exit that protects the relationship and the referral. Signals, triage verdicts, and outcomes are logged so the watch itself improves.

included: signal-class watch across tickets, billing, competitors, payments, and business condition
excluded: the save offer construction itself
credit decisions or collections activity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: churn post-mortems, false-positive complaints, or a new signal source becoming available

pros.claim: Triage keeps save energy pointed at churn that can actually be prevented
pros.example: jumping on a gym's third unresolved ticket this month while accepting that a retiring barber's shop closure is a farewell, not a save

cons.claim: Signal-watching across a whole book generates false positives that can annoy healthy accounts
cons.example: a concerned-sounding call about a single late payment to a twenty-year customer who was simply on vacation

failure_modes: signals sitting unread in ticket history until the port-out request arrives
treating every signal as save-worthy and burning effort on structural churn
no feedback loop, so the same missed-signal pattern repeats each quarter
acceptance_tests: at-risk accounts carry logged signals with a triage verdict (actionable or structural) and a dated next action, and churned accounts show a post-mortem noting which signals were visible beforehand
revisit_triggers: a churn post-mortem finds a signal class the watch does not cover
false-positive rate rises enough to strain customer patience

nodes.definition: Answer actionable churn signals with save plays built strictly inside the agent's actual authority. What the agent can do directly: fix the service problem through escalation muscle, correct the billing error, right-size the plan to what the customer actually needs, redesign the mix (a cheaper primary with a better backup), or add genuine value the program authorizes. What the agent cannot do: discount the carrier's pricing, waive fees, or promise concessions the program has not granted - those routes go to the carrier's retention desk with the agent advocating, and the current program's retention offers are verified in the same cycle they are quoted. Save conversations follow the conduct rules - no fear-selling a wavering customer with exaggerated switching risks - and every save decision weighs viability honestly: a customer whose business is failing is not rescued by a longer contract, and pushing one violates both ethics and clawback sense.

excluded: unauthorized pricing promises
retention of customers whose need for the service has genuinely ended

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: save-play outcomes, retention-offer changes, or a clawback on a saved account

pros.claim: Fixing the actual problem saves more accounts than discounting around it
pros.example: a three-day escalation blitz resolving a cafe's recurring drop-outs, retaining an account no coupon would have kept

cons.claim: Saves that depend on the carrier's retention desk put the outcome outside the agent's control
cons.example: a solid save case dying in a retention queue while the competitor's installer is already scheduled

failure_modes: promising a price the agent has no authority to grant and having the carrier refuse it
quoting a retention offer from memory that the current program no longer runs
fear-selling a wavering customer with inflated claims about switching pain
saving a non-viable account into a term it will disconnect from inside the clawback window
acceptance_tests: every save play documents which lever was used within whose authority, any pricing concession shows a retention-desk route rather than an agent promise, and quoted retention offers carry a same-cycle verification
revisit_triggers: a save fails and the account churns
the program changes retention offers or the retention-desk process
a saved account claws back anyway, questioning the viability call

nodes.definition: Treat churned accounts as a pipeline with rules, not a regret list. Each loss enters with its post-mortem: why it left (price, service pain, relocation, closure, acquisition), what was tried, and when its competitive contract likely ends. Before any win-back effort is spent, the current program's win-back mechanics are verified - many programs treat a returning customer inside a defined window as a reinstatement rather than a new activation, paying differently or not at all, and port-in or same-account rules can change the math entirely. Effort is then sized honestly: a service-pain loss whose pain the carrier has since fixed is a strong candidate at its competitive renewal window; a price-driven loss the program still cannot answer is a courtesy check-in, not a campaign. Any win-back involving a moved address, changed technology, or lapsed equipment routes through re-qualification exactly like a new site.

included: win-back compensation and eligibility verification before effort
honest effort sizing by loss reason
excluded: cold acquisition of never-customers (programs KB)
serviceability assumptions at any returning address

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: win-back outcomes, program re-entry rule changes, or competitor contract intelligence

pros.claim: Verifying win-back mechanics first prevents campaigns that could never have paid
pros.example: discovering a returning customer would re-enter as a reinstatement with no activation event before, not after, three weeks of pursuit

cons.claim: Win-back timing depends on competitor contract dates the agent can only estimate
cons.example: a well-prepared approach landing a year early because the customer's competitive term was longer than assumed

failure_modes: pursuing win-backs without checking re-entry compensation rules
re-quoting a returning site from its old service records instead of re-qualifying the address
spending campaign effort on losses whose driver the program still cannot answer
acceptance_tests: every pursued win-back shows a verified compensation and eligibility check, a loss-reason-based effort rationale, and re-qualification routing when the site or technology changed
revisit_triggers: the program changes win-back or reinstatement rules
a loss reason the program could not answer becomes answerable through new offers

nodes.definition: Be the customer's first call on purpose, and run that position honestly. Intake takes every customer-reported issue - outage, slow speeds, billing question, equipment trouble, a confusing carrier letter - logs it against the account, and triages it: what the agent resolves directly (equipment guidance, billing-question interpretation, expectation-setting), what goes to the carrier with the agent driving (network trouble, provisioning errors, billing corrections), and what the customer must do with the carrier personally (identity verification, payment arrangements, account-security actions the carrier will only take with the account holder). The triage script includes the affiliation truth stated plainly - the agent sells and supports as the carrier's partner; the carrier operates the network and owns the retail account - so being maximally helpful never slides into impersonating authority the agent does not have. Every intake gets an expectation: what happens next, who is doing it, and when the customer hears back.

excluded: operating carrier systems the agent has no access to
any implication of being the carrier

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: customer confusion patterns, support-model changes in the program, or intake issues bypassing the log

pros.claim: Being the trusted first call is the relationship position that renewals and referrals grow from
pros.example: an accountant who calls the agent about a confusing carrier notice before calling anyone else, because the last three answers were fast and straight

cons.claim: First-call position means absorbing the customer's frustration for problems the agent cannot directly fix
cons.example: a week of angry calls during a regional carrier outage the agent can only report and track

failure_modes: letting the customer believe the agent is the carrier because correcting them feels unhelpful
issues taken in but never logged, so patterns invisible to churn watch
no expectation set at intake, generating a second angrier call
acceptance_tests: every intake shows a logged issue, a triage category, an affiliation-honest framing where relevant, and a communicated next step with owner and timeframe
revisit_triggers: an intake pattern shows customers systematically confused about who does what
triage boundaries shift because the program's support model changes

nodes.definition: Know and work the carrier's escalation machinery better than the customer ever could - that skill is a large part of what the customer keeps the agent for. Map each carried program's paths: the partner support line versus retail support, the provisioning-fallout queue, the billing-adjustment process, the network-trouble tiers and what evidence moves a ticket up one, and the named channel or partner manager for when process stalls. Working a ticket means opening it with complete evidence (account identifiers, observed symptoms, business impact stated factually), tracking it with reference numbers and timestamps, escalating on a schedule rather than on frustration, and closing the loop with the customer at each state change. The trail matters twice over: it resolves the issue faster, and it becomes evidence when the issue later feeds a churn save, a dispute, or a service-credit request on the customer's behalf.

excluded: commissions disputes (separate channel)
promising resolution times the carrier has not committed to

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: channel restructures, stalling ticket classes, or partner-manager changes

pros.claim: A mapped escalation path resolves in days what a customer alone waits weeks on hold for
pros.example: routing a stuck provisioning-fallout ticket straight to the partner queue with the order reference the retail line would never have asked for

cons.claim: Escalation capital is finite - burning the partner manager on routine tickets dulls the tool for real emergencies
cons.example: the named contact who stops answering after being pinged for every slow-speed complaint

failure_modes: opening tickets with thin evidence that guarantees a first-round bounce
escalating on anger instead of schedule and burning channel goodwill
no reference trail, so the follow-up call starts from zero every time
promising the customer a resolution time the carrier never committed to
acceptance_tests: every escalated issue carries a complete evidence pack, reference numbers with a timestamped trail, a scheduled next escalation step, and customer updates at each state change
revisit_triggers: the program restructures its support or escalation channels
a ticket class repeatedly stalls at the same tier

nodes.definition: Handle service incidents as the account-level trust events they are. During an outage: confirm whether the wireless backup actually engaged (the register says the site has one; the event proves whether it worked), communicate what is known and unknown factually without over-promising restoration times, and keep the customer informed on a rhythm so silence never becomes the second injury. After restoration: run a short post-event review - what failed, whether failover carried the load the business needed, what the carrier's incident explanation was - and write it to the register. The aftermath is the honest moment to fix real gaps: a backup that never engaged routes to the activation process for re-testing as a defect; a site with no backup that just ate a costly outage deserves a factual conversation about one. What the aftermath is never used for is fear-selling - the recommendation must trace to what actually happened at this site, not to dramatized catastrophe.

included: post-event review written to the register
excluded: failover reconfiguration and re-testing work (activation KB)
dramatizing outage risk to force upgrades

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: incident outcomes, failover-verification failures, or feedback that outage communication fell short

pros.claim: A well-communicated outage often strengthens the relationship more than uneventful uptime
pros.example: a pharmacy that renewed early specifically citing how it was kept informed through a half-day fiber cut while its card terminals ran on backup

cons.claim: High-touch outage communication does not scale during a regional event hitting many accounts at once
cons.example: forty affected accounts and one agent when a flood takes out a central office

failure_modes: going quiet mid-outage and letting silence compound the damage
assuming the backup engaged because the register says one exists
turning a customer's outage pain into a pressure pitch instead of a factual review
no post-event write-back, so the next renewal conversation forgets the event
acceptance_tests: every material incident shows a communication log, a backup-engagement verification, a post-event review written to the register, and any follow-on recommendation traceable to observed facts of that event
revisit_triggers: an incident reveals a failover defect or an uncovered site
a regional event exposes the communication model's scale limits

nodes.definition: Grow existing accounts into additional compensated streams by riding lifecycle moments, not by cold-pitching a catalog. The natural openings: a review that surfaces a real gap (no backup on a site that cannot tolerate downtime, aging phones, a camera need mentioned in passing), a renewal that reopens design anyway, a refresh event that already has the customer thinking about technology, a new location the customer mentions (which routes through site qualification like any new site), and a well-resolved escalation that just demonstrated the agent's value. Every attach must pass three gates: a documented need traceable to the customer's own situation, current-program authorization for the product, and disclosure-first presentation of what the addition commits the customer to. The initial bundle-architecture methodology belongs to the programs KB; this node is the existing-account expansion motion that compounds one relationship into several streams over years.

included: lifecycle-moment openings (review, renewal, refresh, new location, resolved escalation)
excluded: initial bundle architecture and discovery methodology (programs KB)
quota-driven attach pushes with no documented need

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: attach outcomes, catalog changes, or churn analysis on expanded accounts

pros.claim: Lifecycle-triggered attaches close on trust already earned and churn less than cold-pitched ones
pros.example: adding backup wireless to a veterinary clinic the month after an outage review showed exactly what downtime cost it

cons.claim: Waiting for lifecycle moments grows slower than aggressive catalog pushing
cons.example: a quarter where stable accounts offered no natural openings and expansion numbers show it

failure_modes: attaching services with no documented need and generating regret churn plus clawbacks
quoting a new location without routing it through address-level qualification
selling a product the current program no longer authorizes
using an outage's emotional aftermath as a pressure lever instead of a factual basis
acceptance_tests: every expansion attach documents the need it traces to, a same-cycle authorization check, a disclosure-first close, and qualification routing for any new site
revisit_triggers: attach-driven churn or clawback suggests needs were manufactured
the program's product catalog or attach compensation mechanics change

nodes.definition: Roll the account-level data up into the book-level view that steers where lifecycle effort goes. The dashboard reads the ledger and reconciliation history to show: the mechanism mix (how much of the book's compensation is one-time activation versus durable residual versus account-based - an activation-heavy mix means the operator is hunting, not compounding), concentration (share of compensation riding on one carrier, one program, or a handful of anchor accounts), churn and save trends by cohort and cause, in-window clawback exposure, and dispute recovery performance - all expressed as qualitative bands and directional trends, never as invented valuation multiples. The dashboard's job is redirection: a residual mix eroding says work renewals harder; concentration creeping up says the next expansion pushes should favor the under-weighted program; a rising early-churn cohort says fix intake or upstream qualification.

included: churn, clawback, and dispute trend views
excluded: asserting a market value or sale multiple for the book
program entry and exit strategy (programs KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: quarterly roll-ups, threshold crossings, or a mismatch between trends and effort allocation

pros.claim: A mix view catches strategic drift that account-by-account work never surfaces
pros.example: realizing the book's residual share has eroded for three straight quarters because effort chased activation events

cons.claim: Band-level views can mask a single anchor account quietly decaying inside a healthy-looking aggregate
cons.example: a stable overall churn band hiding that the largest multi-site account has opened four tickets and gone quiet

failure_modes: running the book on gut feel until a concentration shock exposes it
letting the dashboard drift into invented precision - specific multiples and projections stated as fact
producing the view but never redirecting effort from it
acceptance_tests: the dashboard shows current mechanism-mix, concentration, churn-trend, clawback-exposure, and dispute-recovery bands with an explicit effort-redirection conclusion each review cycle
revisit_triggers: any band crosses a threshold the operator has set for it
a concentration or churn trend contradicts the current effort allocation

nodes.definition: Protect the book against the risks that live in the agent's own agreements rather than in any customer account. The risk classes: the program amending its compensation plan downward or restructuring mechanisms; minimum-production or activity requirements whose breach suspends or forfeits residuals; termination provisions and what each says about residuals earned before termination (survivability language varies enormously and must be read, not assumed); the master agent or upstream partner being acquired, consolidating, or failing - which can reroute or interrupt the payment path even when the carrier relationship is healthy; and the slow risk of the whole book depending on one agreement's continued goodwill. The responses: know the current agreement's survivability and termination terms as verified fact; keep the evidence trail (orders, activations, statements) that proves what the book earned independently of any portal's continued existence; watch minimum-production status against requirements; and treat rising concentration as a signal to route through program selection for diversification - a decision that belongs to the programs KB, triggered from here.

excluded: selecting or negotiating new programs (programs KB)
legal advice on agreement interpretation (name the question, seek counsel)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: agreement amendments, upstream corporate events, minimum-production drift, or concentration threshold crossings

pros.claim: Knowing survivability terms before a shock turns an existential surprise into a managed event
pros.example: reading the reinstatement and payment-path terms the week a master agent announces its acquisition, instead of the month checks stop

cons.claim: Continuity vigilance can shade into paranoia that sours a healthy working partnership
cons.example: treating a routine plan-version update as an existential threat and escalating it into a strained partner-manager relationship

failure_modes: assuming residuals survive termination because they always have so far
discovering a minimum-production clause only when a suspension notice cites it
keeping all earnings evidence inside a portal the agent loses access to at termination
watching concentration rise for years without ever triggering diversification
acceptance_tests: each carried agreement has verified notes on survivability, termination, and minimum-production terms, an off-portal evidence trail exists for the book's earnings, and concentration crossing the operator's threshold triggers a documented diversification decision
revisit_triggers: an agreement amendment, acquisition announcement, or payment-path change upstream
minimum-production status approaches its requirement
concentration crosses the set threshold

edges.why_related: intake seeds the ledger with each new account's services, plan version, and expected compensation entries
ledger expectations are only meaningful when referenced to the verified current plan version
the intake record founds each account's health register entry with contract dates, equipment, and install notes
reconciliation matches carrier statements against the ledger's plan-referenced expectations
disputes are filed from classified reconciliation variances, not from raw suspicion
clawback window status per entry lives in the ledger that exposure tracking reads
the radar's term and auto-renew dates come from the register's contract data
the radar's work-back schedule opens each renewal play with time to verify and disclose
renewal plays are built on same-cycle verified offers and renewal compensation mechanics
refresh events are mapped to affected accounts through the register's equipment and technology data
reviews start from the register's usage, ticket, and change history and write findings back to it
churn signals are read from the register's ticket, payment, and account-change patterns
save plays answer triaged actionable signals; without triage they fire blind or late
intake logs issues against the register and triages with the account's history in view
issues triaged as carrier-side flow into the partner-channel escalation machinery
outage events enter through intake and are handled with its logging and expectation discipline
expansion attaches trace to documented needs surfaced in honest account reviews
the mix, concentration, and exposure bands roll up from ledger entries
concentration and mix bands are the inputs that continuity risk assessment and diversification triggers read
authorization checks and forfeiture classes are read from the verified current agreement
a clean compliance record is the precondition for residual survivability arguments if the agreement ever ends
save offers may only use levers the current program authorizes; pricing concessions route to the retention desk
every attach must pass a current-program authorization check before it is offered
win-back approaches must be disclosure-first and free of pressure on a customer who already chose to leave once
post-outage recommendations must trace to observed facts, never to dramatized fear of the next failure
aggressive saves keep shaky accounts alive inside clawback windows, extending exposure the containment work is trying to shrink
edges.resolution_rule: save only accounts whose churn driver is fixable and whose business is viable; a non-viable account is released cleanly rather than locked into a term likely to disconnect inside the window

edges.why_related: stream-growth pressure pushes toward attaching services while conduct rules demand documented need and plain disclosure
edges.resolution_rule: conduct wins unconditionally: no documented need traceable to the customer's situation means no attach, whatever the growth target says

edges.why_related: pressing commissions disputes hard strains the same partner relationship the agent needs responsive for customer-service escalations
edges.resolution_rule: keep the channels separate and the tone evidence-led: commissions disputes go through the commissions desk with complete evidence, customer tickets through partner support, and neither is used as leverage in the other

edges.why_related: locking a long renewal term now can strand the account when an imminent refresh or overbuild would change the right design
edges.resolution_rule: check the refresh horizon before choosing term length; when a credible refresh event is near, prefer the shorter term or a refresh-aligned play even at lower immediate commitment

edges.why_related: missed first-bill errors and absent onboarding touches cause the early cancels that trigger most clawbacks
how an outage is handled and communicated directly drives whether the account emerges as a churn risk or a strengthened relationship
well-handled escalations build the demonstrated-value trust that expansion conversations draw on later
a failed save closes with a post-mortem that enters the account into the win-back pipeline with its loss reason
intake schedules the first review, starting the cadence that carries the account through its life
cohort churn trends from the book view re-aim the watch at the segments and signal classes currently bleeding
loss post-mortems reveal which save levers failed and why, improving the next save play's design
a recurring variance pattern is often the first evidence of an unannounced plan change, forcing a terms re-verification
both are standing scan disciplines over the health register - one watches dates, the other watches behavior - and they share cadence infrastructure

conflict_axes.name: save_effort_vs_clawback_containment
conflict_axes.description: Fighting for every at-risk account keeps fragile customers alive inside clawback windows, while strict exposure containment argues for letting non-viable accounts go cleanly.
poles: contain exposure by releasing the non-viable
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: triage on fixability and business viability: fix the fixable with real levers, release the structurally failing without a term lock

conflict_axes.name: activation_chasing_vs_residual_compounding
conflict_axes.description: Activation events pay now and feel like progress; residual durability compounds quietly and pays the book's long-term value - effort allocated to one starves the other.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read the mechanism mix on the dashboard and rebalance deliberately; an eroding residual share is a standing instruction to shift effort to renewals and retention

conflict_axes.name: renewal_lock_vs_refresh_timing
conflict_axes.description: A long term locked today maximizes commitment but can strand the customer on obsolete technology when a retirement or overbuild lands mid-term.
poles: keep terms short around refresh horizons
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: check announced retirements and build-outs against the account before choosing term length; near a credible refresh, shorter or refresh-aligned wins

conflict_axes.name: advocacy_pressure_vs_channel_standing
conflict_axes.description: Pressing the carrier hard - on customer tickets and on commissions disputes - gets results, but the same partner relationship funds both, and burning it dulls every future escalation.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: spend escalation capital on schedule and evidence rather than volume and anger; separate the commissions channel from the service channel entirely

conflict_axes.name: expansion_push_vs_needs_honesty
conflict_axes.description: Multi-stream growth is the business model's compounding engine, but pushing attaches past documented need converts trust into regret churn.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let lifecycle moments surface needs and gate every attach on the customer's own situation; growth targets never override the documented-need gate

conflict_axes.name: retention_urgency_vs_no_fear_selling
conflict_axes.description: Save and post-outage conversations carry real urgency, and the temptation is to amplify it with dramatized risks; conduct rules demand urgency claims match verifiable fact.
poles: amplify urgency to close the save
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: ground every urgency claim in what actually happened at this site or what the carrier actually announced; if the facts are not urgent, the conversation is not either

conflict_axes.name: dispute_pursuit_vs_administrative_cost
conflict_axes.description: Chasing every statement variance recovers money and trains the carrier's desk, but line-level pursuit of trivial mismatches costs attention that renewals and saves need more.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always classify everything, but file by materiality and pattern: bundle recurring small variances into systemic cases instead of chasing each line

conflict_axes.name: carrier_concentration_vs_operational_depth
conflict_axes.description: Concentrating the book in one carrier deepens program expertise, tier status, and escalation relationships, but stakes the whole income stream on one agreement's continuity.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set a concentration threshold in advance; crossing it triggers a documented diversification decision through program selection, whatever the depth benefits

conflict_axes.name: customer_advocacy_vs_account_ownership_rules
conflict_axes.description: The customer treats the agent as their guy who handles everything, but under the agency model the carrier owns the retail account and some actions are the account holder's alone.
poles: act as the customer's full proxy
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: advocate to the edge of the program's rules and say plainly where the edge is; never impersonate the customer or the carrier to get past it

edge_cases.description: A residual line for a still-active account simply vanishes from the monthly commission statement
edge_cases.trigger: carrier billing-system migration, account renumbering, or a silent plan reclassification drops the entry
edge_cases.mitigation: cycle-complete reconciliation flags the missing line immediately; the dispute files inside the window with the activation confirmation and plan-version reference attached

edge_cases.description: A customer cancels in the second month after a rocky install, triggering a full activation clawback
edge_cases.trigger: early disconnect inside the clawback window on an account that never got a first-bill review or onboarding touch
edge_cases.mitigation: intake discipline - first-bill review and scheduled early-tenure touches - prevents most such cancels; the clawback is recorded with its cause so the pattern feeds upstream qualification

edge_cases.description: The carrier announces retirement of the legacy circuits under a dozen accounts in the book
edge_cases.trigger: a copper or legacy-technology shutdown notice covering addresses the agent serves
edge_cases.mitigation: enumerate affected accounts from register equipment data, verify the migration compensation class in the current program, and open planned refresh conversations routed through address-level re-qualification

edge_cases.description: An auto-renewal cutoff passes silently and the customer discovers they are locked into a new term
edge_cases.trigger: the radar missed or never carried the cutoff date, or the work-back never opened the conversation
edge_cases.mitigation: own the miss with the customer, pursue whatever remedy the carrier's process allows, and fix the radar gap; silent rollover is logged as a conduct defect even when the customer shrugs

edge_cases.description: A furious customer calls the agent during an outage believing the agent is the carrier and demands restoration
edge_cases.mitigation: state the affiliation truth plainly while taking real ownership of the escalation - open the partner ticket, drive it on schedule, and keep the customer informed so honesty reads as help, not deflection

edge_cases.description: A competitor's fiber build reaches the customer's plaza mid-term and their sales team is door-knocking
edge_cases.trigger: new competitive infrastructure at an address under an active term
edge_cases.mitigation: log the competitive signal, verify what the current program can actually answer with, and have the fit conversation on facts - never promise unauthorized pricing and never trash-talk beyond verifiable comparison

edge_cases.description: The program restructures its compensation plan mid-cycle, changing how renewals pay
edge_cases.trigger: a plan revision effective before the quarter's renewal plays close
edge_cases.mitigation: the change notice triggers same-cycle re-verification; open plays are re-checked against the new mechanics before any customer commitment, and the ledger's expectations re-base from the effective date

edge_cases.description: Saving an at-risk account seems to require a price the agent has no authority to grant
edge_cases.trigger: a save conversation reaching the edge of agent authority
edge_cases.mitigation: route the concession to the carrier's retention desk with the agent advocating, tell the customer honestly whose decision it is, and never promise the outcome in advance

edge_cases.description: A churned customer wants to return two months after leaving, inside the program's re-entry window
edge_cases.trigger: a win-back opportunity arriving before the window where returning accounts pay as new business
edge_cases.mitigation: verify the reinstatement and win-back compensation mechanics first, serve the customer either way, and set effort expectations knowing this return may generate little or no new compensation

edge_cases.description: The master agent through which residuals flow announces it is being acquired
edge_cases.trigger: an upstream corporate event that may reroute or interrupt the payment path
edge_cases.mitigation: re-read survivability and assignment terms immediately, confirm the off-portal evidence trail of the book's earnings is current, and watch the first post-close statements line by line

edge_cases.description: A long-standing customer in visible financial distress asks how to cut their bill
edge_cases.trigger: business hardship surfacing in a review, save, or inbound call
edge_cases.mitigation: right-size down honestly even though it cuts the residual - present the cheaper adequate configuration, document the choice, and keep the relationship that outlasts the hardship

edge_cases.description: Renewal outreach lands while the same account has an open, unresolved service escalation
edge_cases.trigger: the radar's work-back date colliding with an active ticket
edge_cases.mitigation: resolve or visibly own the service issue before any selling; a renewal pushed during active pain reads as tone-deaf and converts a save-able account into a justified departure

workflow.action: Intake each activated account with a first-bill review
workflow.description: Capture services, terms, plan version, and expected compensation; check the first invoice against the quote; schedule the first onboarding touch
workflow.artifact: account intake record with first-bill check
workflow.gate: every activated account has a complete intake record and a passed or corrected first-bill review before lifecycle handover

workflow.action: Verify and register current program terms
workflow.description: Hold the plan-version register current across all carried programs and read change notices the cycle they arrive
workflow.gate: every carried program shows a current plan version and a same-cycle verification date

workflow.action: Build and maintain the compensation ledger
workflow.description: Map every active service to its mechanism class, plan version, expected schedule, and clawback window status
workflow.gate: every active service has a plan-referenced ledger entry with mechanism class and payment state

workflow.action: Stand up the account health register
workflow.description: Record contract dates, equipment generations, ticket and payment history, and keep it current through every account touch
workflow.gate: renewal radar and churn triage can run from the register without external lookup

workflow.description: Match statements to ledger expectations, classify every variance, and respect the dispute-window clock
workflow.gate: no statement cycle unreconciled and no variance aged past its dispute window unfiled

workflow.description: Assemble evidence packs, file through the designated channel inside the deadline, age and escalate open disputes, write outcomes back
workflow.gate: every filed dispute has complete evidence, an in-deadline timestamp, and a live aging status

workflow.description: Track window status per ledger entry, band the aggregate exposure, and run early-tenure care on fragile new accounts
workflow.artifact: in-window exposure view and early-tenure touch schedule
workflow.gate: aggregate exposure is banded and every in-window account has scheduled onboarding touches

workflow.action: Run the renewal radar and design each play
workflow.description: Open each renewal from the work-back schedule with same-cycle offers, usage fit, and a disclosure-first conversation
workflow.artifact: renewal calendar and per-account play sheets
workflow.gate: every renewal play opens before the auto-renew cutoff with verified offers and a documented disclosure-first close
